name: Makina
editorial_article: Mákina emerged in early 1990s Valencia, Spain, as a high-tempo evolution of the local bakalao scene, blending elements of bouncy techno, hard trance, and Eurodance. Producers frequently utilize synthesizers, sequencers, and samplers to achieve its characteristic 150-180 BPM energy. The genre achieved mainstream chart success in Spain during the mid-1990s with hits like Chimo Bayo's 1991 anthem 'Así me gusta a mí' and EX-3's chart-topping singles 'Extres' and 'Ex-P-Cial'. While rooted in Mediterranean club culture, the sound underwent a distinct cultural transplantation to the United Kingdom, becoming a staple of the rave scenes in North East England and Scotland. Its international visibility was further expanded when Newton's track 'Streamline' was featured in a 2006 Pepsi television advertisement starring Jimmy Fallon.
editorial_definition: A high-tempo electronic dance genre originating in Spain, characterized by bouncy, euphoric melodies and 150-180 BPM rhythms.
sonic_markers: 150-180 BPM, synthesizer-heavy, over-the-top happy melodies, hard trance influence
